events_chronological: Rory, a removals man with no plans beyond the day, moves an old man into a nursing home and hangs his photographs for him.
In the same home Rory catches sight of Mara visiting her grandmother, and takes her number out of the sign-in book.
Mara, a pre-med student, is sleeping with the wrestler Vic and living with parents who despise each other.
Rory and Mara meet again on a bus, and she agrees to a night out.
Mara tap-dances on a shop-front step while Rory plays ukulele and sings an old love song.
Vic beats Rory bloody in the street when he finds out about them.
Mara learns she is pregnant by Vic and books a termination.
Mara changes her mind on the table and walks out, and Rory tells her he will raise the child with her.
Rory and Mara marry at a courthouse with her grandmother and a few friends.
Six years later Mara is a nurse, Rory paints houses and drinks from the morning, and their daughter Poppy is five.
The family dog gets out through a gate Mara left open and is killed on the road.
Rory books a night in a cheap themed motel to force the marriage back to life.
Mara's employer offers her a better job at another practice, and Rory takes it badly.
At the motel they drink, fail to reach each other, and Rory pushes for sex Mara does not want.
Mara leaves to answer a call from work, Rory follows her drunk and makes a scene at the practice, and she is fired.
In the car park Mara tells Rory she has nothing left, and he demands to be told how to fix it.
They go back to Mara's father's house, and Rory forces the confrontation in front of Poppy.
Mara tells Rory it is over, and Poppy runs down the street after him begging him not to go.
Rory walks away into the fireworks as Poppy is carried back.
nonlinear_category_reason: Two timelines six years apart alternate scene for scene, both running forward, each courtship scene answering a scene of the collapse.
syuzhet_notes: The film alternates between two timelines about six years apart with no captions, telling them apart only by film stock, hair and light, and it cuts between them so that a scene of the courtship answers a scene of the collapse almost every time. Told-order bullets 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15 and 16 belong to the earlier timeline; the rest are the last two days of the marriage.
fabula_notes: The six years between the wedding and the motel are never shown, so the causes of the collapse have to be inferred from what sits on either side of the gap. Whether the child is the husband's biologically or the wrestler's is raised and deliberately left unanswered.

events.content: The young removals worker hangs a stranger's family photographs with patient attention, revealing a capacity for domestic tenderness before he has a home of his own.

reader: young Rory is attentive, impulsive and uncommitted to a career

events.content: After seeing her visit her grandmother, he uses the sign-in book to turn a passing glimpse into a deliberate pursuit.

Rory: Mara visits a resident at the home
reader: their courtship begins through Rory's boundary-crossing initiative

events.content: She studies for medicine, returns to a combative family home and sleeps with a wrestler whose confidence masks possessiveness.

reader: Mara enters the courtship carrying an existing relationship and a model of marital hostility

events.content: A chance encounter on a bus gives Rory another opening, and Mara accepts a night out despite the instability surrounding both of them.

Rory: Mara is willing to see him
Mara: Rory offers an unplanned alternative to her current life
reader: mutual courtship replaces Rory's one-sided pursuit

events.content: On a closed shopfront she dances while he accompanies her, creating a private performance whose ease will later be set against their inability to speak.

Rory: Mara trusts him enough to be playful in public
Mara: Rory can make ordinary space feel safe
reader: the early relationship is spontaneous and reciprocal

events.content: Learning about the new couple, Vic attacks Rory in the street and turns Mara's transition between relationships into open violence.

Rory: Vic will punish him for the relationship
Mara: her former partner will not accept her choice
reader: the romance begins under coercion rather than clean separation

events.content: The timing identifies Vic as the likely biological father, and Mara books a termination rather than ask either man to decide for her.

reader: the future child begins before Mara and Rory's marriage

events.content: Mara stops the procedure after it has begun, and Rory answers the uncertainty by promising to become the father in practice.

Rory: Mara wants to continue the pregnancy
Mara: Rory will claim the parental role
reader: their family is founded on Rory's promise rather than biological certainty

events.content: With only a few witnesses and Mara's grandmother, the couple formalise the promise before the child is born.

reader: the marriage follows directly from the pregnancy and Rory's commitment

events.content: Mara supports patients as a nurse while Rory paints houses, drinks early and treats time with Poppy as the centre of a life that has otherwise stalled.

reader: the loving courtship has become an unequal and exhausted marriage

questions.q1: what was Rory like before the stalled life shown in the present?
questions.q2: how did Rory and Mara first enter one another's lives?
questions.q4: how did the young couple become parents before the life shown in the present?
questions.q6: can the marriage survive the present crisis?

events.content: An open gate leads to a body beside the traffic, giving grief and blame a concrete form at the start of the couple's final two days.
events.location: the road outside the family home

reader: Mara and Rory meet shared grief with blame rather than comfort

events.content: He treats privacy, alcohol and forced novelty as a repair plan, while Mara agrees to go without sharing his confidence that one night can restore them.

Mara: Rory believes a motel night can revive the marriage
reader: Rory responds to structural problems with a staged romantic gesture

questions.q7: will the motel night repair anything between them?

events.content: A professional opportunity gives Mara a possible independent future, and Rory hears it as evidence that her life is moving away from him.

Mara: another practice offers her better work
Rory: Mara may change jobs without him
reader: Mara's growth intensifies Rory's fear of abandonment

events.content: Alcohol strips away the motel fantasy; Rory presses for sex while Mara withdraws, making physical intimacy another argument about obligation.

Rory: Mara does not want the intimacy he planned
Mara: Rory will push past her refusal
reader: the attempted repair reproduces the marriage's coercion

questions.q3: were Rory and Mara ever capable of easy intimacy?

events.content: When Mara answers a work call and leaves, he follows drunk, confronts her employer and converts his fear into the loss of her job.

Mara: Rory's behaviour has cost her employment
reader: Rory damages the independent future he feared

events.content: In the car park she says there is no feeling left to restore, while Rory insists that a solvable task must still exist.

Rory: Mara believes the marriage is beyond repair
reader: the couple no longer agrees that love is a problem with a technique

questions.q5: why does Rory believe commitment means there must still be something to fix?

events.content: At Mara's father's house he refuses a private separation and makes Poppy witness the adults' competing claims about home and parenthood.

reader: Rory's refusal to leave quietly makes Poppy bear the conflict

events.content: She states the decision without another repair condition, and Poppy runs after Rory as he begins to leave the family she knows.
events.location: the street outside Mara's father's house

reader: the separation that shadowed the present timeline becomes explicit

questions.q8: will Rory stay when Poppy begs him not to go?

events.content: Fireworks turn his retreat into bright fragments behind him while Poppy is carried in the opposite direction, separating romantic image from family consequence.

reader: the story ends with Rory outside the family role he once volunteered to take
